description.narrative: The project aims to develop a sustainable herbal tea value chain by strengthening the linkages between the cooperative and local communities cultivating native medicinal flowers in Khanh Yen, Lao Cai. It seeks to establish clean and organic raw material zones, replacing low-yield crops, and enhancing the cooperative’s capacity for sustainable production, green processing, and digital transformation. In addition, the project focuses on building a strong brand and expanding markets both domestically and internationally, while empowering ethnic minority women through stable and meaningful employment. Specifically, the project intends to increase the income and secure employment for ethnic minority women to a level of 7–9 million VND per month, promote circular and green economy practices at the local level, encourage environmentally friendly cultivation using organic fertilizers derived from agricultural by-products, and develop experiential tourism linked to local products. Furthermore, it aims to improve and diversify herbal tea products, targeting a revenue increase of 25–30 percent. Key activities of the project include organizing an initial workshop to introduce the project, raise awareness, and mobilize local farmers to participate in cultivating flowers such as chrysanthemum and rose for herbaltea. The project will establish interest-based farmer groups, provide training on group management, meeting organization, sustainable cultivation techniques, organic composting, and the use of high-quality flower seedlings. Support will also be provided for official registration of planting zones, facilitating contracts between the cooperative and farmer groups, and upgrading processing facilities, including tea packaging, solar-powered drying systems, and labeling equipment. Additional activities involve training in green tea processing techniques, multi-channel marketing, digital branding, and participation in trade fairs and promotional events. Community engagement components include workshops on labor division in households and communities and competitions showcasing gender equality and women’s economic leadership linked with sustainable tea production. The project will be implemented from January 2026 to June 2027 in Khanh Yen commune, Lao Cai province, with the cooperative Van An serving as the production, processing, and training hub. Beneficiaries include at least 120 ethnic minority women and households participating in flower cultivation and herbal tea production, while the cooperative, consumers, and the broader community will benefit from enhanced production capacity, market access, andsustainable livelihoods.

participating-org.narrative: The Lao Cai Cooperative Alliance (LCA) is the representative organization for cooperatives, cooperative unions, cooperative groups,and other collective economic entities operating in Lao Cai Province, Vietnam. Established as a legal entity with its own seal and bank account, LCA operates in accordance with Vietnamese law and its official charter. The Alliance’s main functions include representing and safeguarding members’ rights and interests; disseminating Party guidelines, State policies, and laws onthe collective economy; participating in policy development and proposing support programs and projects for cooperatives; providing consulting, technical assistance, and public services to members; and fostering collaboration, linkage, and mutual supportamong members. LCA’s key responsibilities are guiding members in implementing Party and State policies, coordinating with government departments, agencies, and social organizations to implement development programs, gathering members’ feedback to submitrecommendations to authorities, organizing training and capacity-building activities, promoting emulation movements, and mobilizing legal domestic and international resources to support the development of cooperatives. With many years of experience, LCAcontinues to strengthen cooperatives’ management capacity, market access, and application of science and technology for sustainable development. Through its work, the Alliance contributes to building a dynamic, efficient, and inclusive cooperative sectorin Lao Cai Province.
